I bought an external drive to back up my MacBook Air, which runs macOS Sonoma. How do I set it up for Time Machine?

1. Plug in an external drive with at least twice your Mac's storage, and use it only for backups.
2. From the **Apple** menu, choose **System Settings**.
3. Click **General** in the sidebar, then click **Time Machine** on the right.
4. Click **Add Backup Disk**, or click the **Add** button.
5. Select your connected storage device, then click **Set Up Disk**.
6. If your Mac asks to erase the drive, either erase it or select a different backup disk or volume.
7. If your Mac asks whether to claim backups from another computer, claim them if you want them to become part of this Mac's backups.
8. If you turn on **Encrypt Backup**, you will be asked to create a backup password. You will need it if you later restore files from the backup.

Set the date and time automatically on your iPhone:
1. Make sure that your device is connected to the internet.
2. Install the latest software updates for your device.
3. Open Settings, tap **General**, tap **Date & Time**, then turn on **Set Time Automatically**.
4. If a message says that updated time zone information is available, restart your device and any paired Apple Watch.
5. Open Settings, tap **Privacy & Security**, tap **Location Services**, scroll to the bottom and tap **System Services**, then turn on **Setting Time Zone**.
Set Time Automatically might not be available with all carriers or in all countries and regions. If the device has a Screen Time passcode or a corporate profile with device restrictions installed, the setting might be dimmed (grayed out).

Here is how to set up Medical ID on your iPhone so paramedics can find it.
1. Open the **Health** app and tap the **Summary** tab.
2. Tap your profile picture in the upper corner.
3. Tap **Medical ID**.
4. Turn on **Show When Locked** to make Medical ID available from the Lock screen.
5. Turn on **Share During Emergency Call** to share it with emergency responders. It is then shared automatically when you call or text emergency services from iPhone or Apple Watch.
6. Tap **Edit** or **Add** next to a field, such as medications, allergies, or conditions, to update it.
7. Tap **Done**.
If you turn off **Emergency Calls & SOS**, your Medical ID information will not be shared. That setting is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services.

Got an email from a debt collector with a link to pay an old debt. Is it real?

I asked for validation and they sent back a notice with a gift card code to pay, and the name on it isn't mine. What do I do?

Don't pay with that gift card code. Anyone who insists that you pay by gift card is always a scammer.

1. If the debt isn't yours, or you don't recognize it, send the debt collector a dispute letter within 30 days of getting the validation information.
2. Say you don't owe some or all of the money, and ask for verification of the debt.
3. Keep a copy of the letter for your records.
4. If you spot a fake or abusive debt collector, report it to your state attorney general's office and the Federal Trade Commission.

1. In the **Find My** app, go to the **Devices** tab.

5. If you want to show your contact information on the device, follow the onscreen steps.

If Stolen Device Protection is on, Face ID or Touch ID is required to turn off Lost Mode, even if someone knows your passcode.

I have low vision and small text is hard for me to read, so please give me the fewest steps. My Windows 11 PC says the disk space is low.

Here are the fewest steps to free up space on your Windows 11 PC.
1. Select **Start**, then **Settings**, then **System**, then **Storage**, then **Cleanup recommendations**.
2. Review the categories **Temporary files**, **Large or unused files**, **Files synced to the cloud**, and **Unused apps**, then choose the items you want to remove.
3. Click the **Clean up** button in each section.
If you upgraded Windows fewer than 10 days ago, your previous version appears as a deletable system file. Deleting it removes the Windows.old folder, which contains files that give you the option to go back to your previous version of Windows. If you delete your previous version of Windows, this can't be undone.

My Chromebook screen is too small for me to read my email. Everything looks tiny. How do I make the whole screen bigger? I'm not good with computers, so simple steps please.

Here is how to make your whole Chromebook screen bigger:
1. Select the time at the bottom right, or press **Alt + Shift + S**.
2. Select **Settings**, then **Accessibility**.
3. Under **Display**, turn on **Full screen magnifier**.
4. Choose how the magnified view moves with your mouse: **Move screen continuously as mouse moves**, **Move screen keeping mouse at center of screen**, or **Move screen when mouse touches edge of screen**.
5. To increase magnification, press **Ctrl + Alt + Brightness up**. To decrease it, press **Ctrl + Alt + Brightness down**.

My iPhone 13 won't charge at all, even with a brand new cable.

Try these steps in order:
1. Plug the iPhone into a computer, a power accessory, or a wall outlet.
2. Restart the iPhone.
3. Check the charging cable and USB adapter for damage, such as breaks or bent prongs. Stop using any damaged accessory.
4. Use a wall outlet, make sure the cable, USB adapter, and outlet connect securely, or try a different outlet.
5. Clear debris from the charging port on the bottom of the iPhone, then firmly plug in the cable.
6. Leave it charging.
7. If it still won't turn on or shows a battery icon on the screen, force a restart.
8. On iPhone 8 or later, quickly press **volume up**.
9. Quickly press **volume down**.
10. Press and hold the **side button** until the Apple logo appears.

If it still won't turn on or charge, you may need service through the 'Get service' link.

Here is the quickest way to turn on Wi-Fi calling on your Android phone.

I think my iPhone should use Wi-Fi calling at home, but calls still drop. What can I do?

I already called my carrier and they said it's supported. I restarted my iPhone and turned Wi-Fi Calling on, but I still can't make a Wi-Fi call at home.

Try these steps next.
Wait two minutes before you go from one step to the next.

2. Open the **Settings** app and tap **Cellular**.
3. If your iPhone has multiple SIMs, tap the line you want to use.
4. Tap **Wi-Fi Calling**.
5. Turn **Wi-Fi Calling** off and then on again.
6. Go back to **Settings** and tap **General**.
7. Tap **Transfer or Reset iPhone**, then tap **Reset**.
8. Tap **Reset Network Settings**.

I'm visiting a friend and need to get my iPhone onto their wifi. How do I join it?

Here is how to join a Wi-Fi network on your iPhone.
1. Open **Settings** and select **Wi-Fi**, then switch **Wi-Fi** on.
2. Select the network you want.
3. If the network asks for a password or its terms and conditions, enter the password or accept the terms. If you don't know the password, ask your network administrator.
4. Check for a blue tick beside the network name and the **Wi-Fi** icon in the top corner of the screen. This confirms the connection.
5. Optional: For a more reliable connection that uses cellular data alongside Wi-Fi, scroll down and turn on **Connectivity Assist**.
